News.title: Chorizo and pepper ‘remembered rice’
News.content:
This is an approximation of the rice dish that’s served at nearly every beach bar on the Algarve. It was one of my dad’s favourite dishes. He used to kind of growl when the bowls of it arrived.

This is as near to the dish we loved as possible. I did wonder whether it contained cumin – maybe it did in some places – so you could add half a teaspoon to the vegetables.

You could also add half a teaspoon of Marmite to the stock. The dish tasted quite beefy in some places but the addition is up to you. If you don’t have enough chicken stock, add water to make the liquid up to 750ml.

News.content: It’s hard to shift notions about food that you acquire as a child. Despite living on the coast, my family regarded prawns and crab as a big treat. But while they’re not cheap, you really can stretch them out to make delicious everyday dishes.

News.title: Summer strawberry and elderflower cake
News.content:

Whisked sponges are properly made by beating the eggs and sugar over a pan of simmering water, but it’s a bit of a palaver. Don’t assemble it until just before serving.

News.title: Gadget Show host Jason Bradbury:‘I don’t like seeing kids in restaurants staring at an iPad’
News.content:
We’ve covered an extensive amount of technology here at Telegraph Recommended, from the latest smartphones and laptops to voice-activated kitchen bins. There are a lot of products on the market, but one person who knows how to sort the wheat from the chaff is Jason Bradbury.

The tech expert is best known for presenting Channel 5’s technology programme The Gadget Show for 12 years. He’s also the author of a series of techno-thrillers for children, and has also been on the judging panels for the BAFTA Video Games Awards and the MediaGuardian Innovation Awards.

We sat down with Bradbury at the Ideal Home Show in Birmingham, where he curated the smart home showcase, for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer queries from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel. Read his answers below.

Is there a best time of year to purchase new gadgets?

Boris, North West

Yes. Often, new technology is showcased in January and is sometimes revisited in summer, then is available to buy in the autumn. That means September, October or November is the best time to buy new tech, like games consoles, virtual reality helmets or new smartphones.

If you were on a desert island, which gadget would you miss the most?

My Onewheel. As the name suggests, it’s a single wheel with a skateboard built around it. It’s the closest you’ll get to being like Marty McFly in Back To The Future. At the ripe age of 57 years old, this is my daily driver. When I’ve taken my kids to school, I jump on my skateboard and glide down into town. I live in Newquay, Cornwall, and while you can go on the beach with it, it’s got to be a flat beach. A desert island isn’t going to be ideal.

Do you prefer iPhone or Android devices?

This is a political question for which 50 per cent of the population are going to hate me. In fact, a larger proportion of people actually have Android devices.

I love both for different reasons, and both have amazing features to offer. The walled garden that is the iPhone is a coherent operating system, but you can’t put stuff on or get stuff off it easily, which Android is great for.

Are we pushing technology into areas of the home that don’t need it?

Anthony, Yorkshire

There’s nothing wrong with an AI feature-rich bird table. We may be pushing technology into areas of the home that it never belonged in, but it’s a choice. We get pressured to buy the shiniest new thing, but it’s easy to go off grid. I have a campervan, and while yes I plug it in to charge the battery, it’s pretty much off grid. I could take an Xbox with me, but I don’t.

If you choose to buy technology that enhances life for you, that’s great. Take the bird feeder – one I saw at the Ideal Home Show, for example, uses AI to identify the species of bird that’s nibbling on the seeds that you put out. If you’re not as mobile as you used to be, you get to interact with your garden in a way that you wouldn’t ordinarily be able to. Someone else would say that was a ridiculous idea.

It’s an exciting time. I like where smart tech is going. In the health area, it could be seen as an intrusion, collecting the most intimate data around your body. But it’s important to know where your health is so you can take action and own it.

What are your tech predictions for the next few years?

Brian, London

AI is going to bring us new materials. There will be efficiency gains in the recovery of thermal energy, with benefits for fuel efficiency. We’ll see new types of polymers and non-polluting plastics, with gains through AI in biology to make organisms that can consume plastic. This will hopefully solve microplastic pollution – a dreadful problem in Cornwall. There will also be advances in surgery, identifying disease in treatment and pharmacology.

I understand people’s jobs are at risk from AI, and that’s a real consequence. But if you stop the cynicism for a minute, it is an incredible moment in our history. I feel privileged to be gazing through the window of the next two years and beyond. We could be looking at fusion reactors efficient enough to work properly, self-driving vehicles that will make travel safer and more efficient, new fuels… It’s mind-blowing.

When did your interest in tech begin?

Daniel, London

My father, who was a plastics expert working for a factory, brought home a prototype for the first generation of digital watches and calculators.

I was born in 1969, and it was an amazing time to be alive. Growing up and being conscious of tech in the 70s and 80s felt similar to how it does now. The ‘70s was quite analogue before the mass adoption of consumer electronics, computers and video games. The fervour around new ideas, born of the obsession and efficiency gains with AI, is a similar feeling to the 80s.

Who was your biggest inspiration?

Ekaterina, West Midlands

My father. He was a huge fan of technology and insisted on buying me computers and first-generation consoles. He got me to try programming and be connected to the world in which he was making prototypes for the new computer generation.

There’s also Sir Clive Sinclair, who was the ‘80s answer to Elon Musk, if Elon Musk was ginger and looked like a geography teacher. He was the brains behind the first computer that a lot of British kids in the 80s got their hands on, the ZX80, ZX81 and the ZX Spectrum. I actually own the Sinclair C5 vehicle from 1985, although I don’t drive it too often because it’s not that reliable.

Does having a smart home pose any security risks?

Liam, London

Yes. When you install cameras and smart devices that track you, there is, without a shadow of a doubt, a consideration there around who does what with that data. When everything’s connected, someone can hack it. There are efforts every minute of every day to grab your personal information to monetise it. You need to consider that, especially with AI, which is great at writing code, hacking and putting that power in the hands of all kinds of people.

What I’d say on that score is to get a router with good security, and don’t go with default passwords.

What’s your ‘take’ on children and gadgets?

Patricia, West Midlands

As the father of three crazy young people, one of whom is a professional Fortnite player, I have an open attitude to technology. But I also don’t like seeing kids in restaurants staring at an iPad. I also understand the pressures that parents have and I’m guilty of doing the same thing. Sometimes you’ve been up all night with a baby, so your toddler gets the iPad instead of you.

I don’t think people need me to patronise them and tell them what they already know, which is that technology is empowering, wonderful and fun, but when it’s sunny outside, get out there and get dirty. It’s all about balance.

News.title: They seek riches from the jungle – but this eco-system is our future
News.content:
As the sun sinks over the Sangha river in a far corner of the Congo Basin, the village chief contemplates the future of his homeland. “The resources will finish, but after that, then what?” asks Gabriel Mobolambi. His village, Bomassa, is the gateway to Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park – a vast stretch of largely unspoilt jungle.

Like many who live in this remote region, he has had to weigh up the benefits of resource exploitation against conservation. The region is rich in precious metals and gems which promise riches – but Mobolambi, a responsible leader, takes a longer view.

“There are gold and diamonds in the forest, but conservation is dependable,” he says. Behind him, fishermen cast their nets into the fast-flowing water. Mobolambi is part of a network of indigenous communities who believe that conserving their pristine environment is a safer bet for long-term prosperity. Their work has ramifications that could extend well beyond this vast wilderness.

Gabriel Mobolambi, the chief of Bomassa village, on the boundary of Nouabalé-Ndoki Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham Elephants bathe at the Mbeli bai forest clearing, the site of a long term scientific survey Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham

The tributaries of the Congo River system reach into nine countries; its twists and turns nourish forests and swamps that trap more carbon than even the Amazon region. It is in the Republic of Congo that these jungles are at their most impressive, covering well over half of the country and sheltering endangered species.

The region has known decades of insecurity. Mobolambi still remembers the 1997 civil war, when armed militias from across central Africa would arrive to hunt elephants amid the chaos, exchanging gifts with local chiefs for the right to leave with plundered ivory. “It was a strange conflict,” he says, “but now we wear the same scent.”

Research groups monitor the bais, which reveal wildlife that is usually hidden in the dense forest Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham/The Telegraph

Despite this new calm, in the past two decades, the Republic of Congo has lost over a million hectares of tree cover.

Walking with a research team, we leave the village of Bomassa on foot. The terrain is difficult, and a few miles into the permanent shadows of the tall tree canopy it swiftly turns into a muddy endurance sport. Researchers, including Aristide Mouele of Wildlife Conservation Society, from the coastal city of Pointe-Noire, often have to use canoes to access campsites deep in the jungle.

“These ecosystems create the second lung of the world,” explains Mouele, who has been working at Nouabalé-Ndoki since 2017, running a study project at one of the park’s natural forest clearings, known locally as bais.

Our movement from a campsite to an observation platform at the bai must be made in watchful groups, and only in daylight hours, with all eyes kept peeled for any elephants that could be startled and charge.

Arriving in the open bai reveals a world of life that would be invisible in the undergrowth.

Western lowland gorillas cautiously peer out from the treeline, then roll into the thick fronds of grass, while groups of forest elephants greet each other with excitable flapping of trunks and tails.

A river flows through the bai, and a crocodile can suddenly be seen gliding through the clearing.

This bai has been monitored since way back in 1995, and every individual animal visiting the area has been logged. “The animals maintain the ecosystem,” says Mouele. “The bai is a summary of the health of the forest.”

A forest elephant moves through the jungle of Nouabale-Ndoki Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham An infant western lowland gorilla in the jungle close to the Mondika research camp Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham

Elephants that graze here spread seeds throughout the Congo Basin, as they pass across international borders.

Though emblematic species such as gorillas, chimpanzees and forest elephants attract the most interest and funding, researchers on the ground still find time for less glamorous yet critical climate science. Mouele’s project, a study of animal behaviour, is a labour of love, and he has spent countless nights sleeping on a spartan observation deck, eating tinned rations and sheltering from rainstorms.

Other long-term studies are underway here to assess the health of the forest. At the twin research sites of Mondika and Goualougo, both in the Nouabalé-Ndoki park, around 1,000 individual trees are visited and inspected each month, a painstaking process that requires up to six days of hiking in the forest and minute observations, tallying leaves and fallen fruits, recording growth, scars and signs of disease.

Researcher Gaston Abea walks through a swarm of butterflies at the Mondika research campsite Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham Tracker Nelson Mobolambi, the village chief ’s son, manoeuvres his canoe Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham

The study’s remit is to reveal long-term trends, and its data will highlight the effects of changing temperatures on fruiting, flowering and seed dispersal.

While Mouele was trained at the Marien Ngouabi University in Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of Congo, the majority of the trackers who work at the park are from Ba’aka indigenous hunter-gatherer communities, the original inhabitants of the region.

A forest elephant moves through the jungle – researchers must be careful not to startle them Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham/The Telegraph

Gaston Abea is a Ba’aka, and the first member of an indigenous community to become a published academic author, for his observations of gorilla behaviour in the forests of Nouabalé-Ndoki. “The forest is our school of life,” he says. “I have six children and will bring them all here to learn the traditions of our ancestors.”

The jungle seems less impenetrable when he walks through it, pointing out herbs and shoots that have medical uses. “We can spend 21 days in the forest, we carry 20kg packs and stop every 500 metres to map all the species of tree and animal we see or any damage,” explains Abea.

These indigenous communities have long been marginalised and targeted during conflicts across the Congo Basin. Over 60,000 Mbuti pygmies were killed in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) during the Second Congo War in the early 2000s.

Working in conservation has helped keep the culture of these groups alive; their traditional survival skills and ability to navigate the forests are of vital importance for modern research.

The low population density of the Republic of Congo has saved it from many of the issues faced in DRC, where millions more are dependent on the shrinking resources of the land.

Trackers hike through the forests of Nouabale-Ndoki Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham A barge carrying hundreds of logs travels downstream on the Congo river. Credit : Hugh Kinsella Cunningham

Industrial exploitation is increasing though, and the road that leads from Nouabalé-Ndoki to the trading town of Ouesso is lined with flatbed trucks piled with bulbous logs. Along the Congo River, barges can frequently be seen travelling with hundreds of cut trees destined for sawmills downstream or for sale into opaque supply chains.

Many of the largest old-growth trees here date back 900 years. “These trees are rare, and do not replace easily. They grew when the forest was more open and lighter,” says Dr David Morgan, of Lincoln Park Zoo in Chicago, another of Nouabalé-Ndoki’s visiting researchers.

Conditions have dramatically changed since then, and when they are felled, they will be the last of their kind.

News.title: Oil jumps back above $100 as US and Iran trade missile fire
News.content:
Oil prices rose back above $100 a barrel as the US and Iran exchanged missile fire in the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose as much as 2.9pc to nearly $103 as the fragile ceasefire faced its most serious test.

Crude had dropped down as low as $96 on Thursday but lurched upwards after US forces carried out strikes on Iranian military targets in response to an attack on three American destroyers in the Strait.

Stocks fell sharply overnight, with the main indexes in Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong all down more than 1pc.

President Donald Trump said the strikes on Iran were “just a love tap” and insisted the ceasefire was still in effect.

Iran is yet to announce its response to a US proposal setting out the terms for ending the conflict.

Sports.title: Arsenal Invincibles legend brutally reveals which trophy Mikel Arteta MUST prioritise with Gunners on cusp of Double
Sports.content:
ARSENAL icon Robert Pires has told Mikel Arteta which trophy the club MUST win as they eye an incredible double.

The Gunners booked their spot in the Champions League final following a hard-fought win against Atletico Madrid over two legs, while they also moved five-points clear at the top of the table after Manchester City drew with Everton.





It has put them on the cusp of a first league title for more than 20 years, and a second chance at winning the Champions League for the first time in club history when they take on Paris Saint-Germain on May 30.

Arsenal have missed the feeling of winning silverware for a while, with their last trophy coming with the FA Cup in 2020.

However, Pires, 59, is someone who knows all about the winning feeling in North London, having won two Premier Leagues and FA Cups, including the Invincible season.

French World Cup and European Championship winner Pires was still at Arsenal in their Champions League final defeat to Barcelona in 2006, but was taken off early by Arsene Wenger.



Arsenal look set to repeat that level of success for the first time since Pires left the club, and arguably eclipse it if they can land Europe‘s premier cup competition.

But he has told “friend” Arteta which trophy he absolutely must land this season.

Speaking at a Topps Chrome Collection event in Shoreditch, London on Thursday alongside Myles Lewis-Skelly, Pires said: “This is a very important end of the season, of course.

“They are very close to winning two great trophies, but for me the best one is the Premier League.

“The next game against West Ham is very, very important, as Myles knows.

“It will be very difficult and very tough.

“But I always believe in Arsenal, in the players, and of course in Mikel Arteta because he is my friend.



“I think he has been doing very well for a long, long time.

“So this is, for Myles and the other players, a good opportunity.”

Pires arrived at the event a few minutes behind London lad Lewis-Skelly, whose performance at the Emirates on Tuesday night was instrumental in Arsenal progressing into the final.



Lewis-Skelly was seen taking in the Ballon d’Or trophy before ripping open a few packs of Topps Chrome cards alongside Pires.

And the Englishman was left stunned when Pires found a rare ‘Power Players’ card of Lewis-Skelly in the first pack he opened.

Sports.title: Injuries & suspensions update for Gameweek 35: Latest news on Morgan Gibbs-White, Robert Sanchez and others
Sports.content:
DREAM TEAM brings you all the latest injury, suspension and availability news ahead of Gameweek 35.

Chelsea will be without Robert Sanchez, Pedro Neto and Alejandro Garnacho at Anfield this Saturday lunchtime.



The former is currently the fourth-most popular goalkeeper in Dream Team.

In better news for the Blues, Levi Colwill and Reece James returned to the bench in Gameweek 34 and both defenders have since trained without complaint — Calum McFarlane suggested the pair are pushing to start against Liverpool.



As for the Reds, this weekend comes too soon for Mohamed Salah and Alisson but Giorgi Mamardashvili has a chance of taking the gloves if he completes his first session unscathed.

Alexander Isak partially trained on Thursday and will be considered for selection if he shows he’s capable today.

Elsewhere, 12.6%-owned Morgan Gibbs-White did not feature during Nottingham Forest’s Europa League semi-final defeat to Aston Villa after his nasty head injury at Stamford Bridge required multiple stitches.



However, the in-form midfielder was named on the bench which suggests he is prepared to play while wearing a protective mask if required — Forest host Newcastle on Sunday.

The Magpies will be without Lewis Miley, who fractured his fibula in training this week and will be out of action for “a few months”.

Eddie Howe also expressed doubts about Fabian Schar and Tino Livramento’s availability for the remainder of the season.



Rodri remains a doubt for Manchester City’s double header against Brentford and Crystal Palace but Pep Guardiola is hopeful the midfielder will be able to play some part.

The decorated tactician also spoke positively about Ruben Dias and Josko Gvardiol’s progress during his Friday press conference, suggesting the defenders will feature before the end of the campaign.

Mikel Merino and Jurrien Timber are expected to be Arsenal’s only absentees at West Ham.

Bournemouth released a club statement earlier today to confirm that Alex Jimenez will not be included in Andoni Iraola’s squad to face Fulham while the club investigate a serious matter involving “posts circulating on social media”.

Justin Kluivert is expected to make his return for the Cherries this weekend.



Solly March and James Milner will be available for Brighton against Wolves on Saturday but Diego Gomez is likely to need another week of recovery.

Mats Wieffer is still doubtful for the Seagulls due to a troublesome ankle issue.

Roberto De Zerbi did not reveal any new concerns which suggests Richarlison has shaken off the knock he suffered at Villa Park.

Dominic Solanke is said to be “improving” but isn’t expected to line up against Leeds on Monday night.



In-form Noah Okafor won’t travel with the Whites to North London after incurring a calf strain.

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘could sign Kylian Mbappe by winning the Champions League in history-changing’ transfer coup
Sports.content:
FORMER Arsenal star Emmanuel Petit believes the Gunners could land a “history-changing” transfer coup by winning the Champions League.

The former Arsenal man says a Champions League triumph this summer could tempt Kylian Mbappe to the Emirates.





Petit, a World Cup winner with France in 1998, remains a cult hero at Arsenal after arriving from Monaco in 1997 and helping Arsène Wenger’s side complete a historic Double in 1998.

The ex-midfielder, who famously scored in the 1998 World Cup final, also lifted the FA Cup during his time in North London and is still closely associated with one of Arsenal’s most influential eras.

Now, Petit believes Mikel Arteta’s current side are on the brink of something special after their remarkable run to the Champions League final.

Petit said: “If Arsenal win the Champions League for the first time then it would change the course of their history and send a strong message in the transfer market.”

He added: “Players would of course want to play for the Champions League winners and hope they can go and win it again, it would help them attract Kylian Mbappe if he does leave Real Madrid.”

Arsenal have surged into the final after a string of impressive performances in Europe, with Arteta’s side showing resilience, tactical maturity and attacking threat throughout the competition.

The Gunners’ journey has reignited belief among fans that the club can once again sit at Europe’s top table, with Petit insisting success could transform their transfer power overnight.

And he believes Mbappe, currently at Real Madrid but reportedly unsettled after over four million fans signed a petition calling for him to leave, would be an ideal fit for the Premier League side.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Petit said: “Arsenal would love Kylian Mbappe and he’d be perfect on their left wing.

“I could also see him at a team like Liverpool as they look to replace the gap left by Mohamed Salah in their team. They have missed Luis Diaz hugely.”

However, Petit doubts the French superstar will leave Madrid any time soon.

“The only reason I think Mbappe will stay at Real Madrid is because if he leaves without winning a trophy it would make his move a failure.



“Mbappe has a huge ego so he will probably want to stay and to prove the opposite. I’m pretty sure about that.

“I don’t see him leaving Madrid, probably the biggest club in the world, unless the decision is made for him.

“The only way he leaves is if Florentino Perez cracks under the pressure.”

Petit then warned that Mbappe’s mentality could also create problems for France at the World Cup if not carefully managed.



Petit told Boyle Sports, who offer the latest Champions League betting: “France have two players actually up front, Michael Olise and Ousmane Dembele.

“Dembele is the Ballon d’Or winner. Olise is with the players who can win the Ballon d’Or at the end of the season. Those guys have been amazing for the last two seasons.”

He added: “Mbappe is playing up front as a striker. Dembele is playing up front as a striker. Ask Didier Deschamps, the French manager, ‘Who is going to play?’”

Petit believes structure is key for France to succeed.



Adding: “If I am Didier Deschamps, for me it’s very simple. Ask Kylian Mbappe to play on the left, the way he was brilliant for years with Paris Saint-Germain.

“Ask Dembele to play up front as a striker, and I ask Olise to play as a right winger.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“If you do like that, I’m pretty sure France will win the World Cup. If you don’t do that and you want to go the same way that Madrid has been doing with Kylian Mbappe then you’re going to have trouble.

“Egos in the dressing room will come out, and the trouble will start in the team.”

Sports.title: Rotherham release THIRTEEN players including ex-Man Utd starlet with economics degree and former £10m Premier League ace
Sports.content:
ROTHERHAM have released THIRTEEN players following their relegation to League Two.

The South Yorkshire outfit dropped out of League One after finishing 23rd in the table.





Rotherham will now start to rebuild their squad in an attempt to gain promotion in the 2026-27 season.

The club has made a start by releasing over a dozen players from the squad.

Dru Yearwood and Shaun McWilliams are yet to discover if options in their contracts will see them continue with the team in League Two.

The news was confirmed in a statement released by the club.

An extract read: “Following careful consideration between a number of departments within the football club, and taking into account the feedback provided by Lee Clark and his assessment of our playing staff towards the latter stages of the 2025/26 campaign, Rotherham United has confirmed it’s retained list.

“No fewer than 11 senior first-team players will depart AESSEAL New York Stadium upon the expiration of their contracts on 30th June.

“The club also places on-record its gratitude to those departing at the end of their contracts with our thanks for their contributions during their stints here in South Yorkshire.”

This cull from the squad includes former Manchester United prospect Duncan Watmore.

Sports.title: ‘Never forgotten it’ – Former Premier League boss reveals Cristiano Ronaldo’s incredible gesture towards late mother
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO was lauded by Brendan Rodgers for a chivalrous gesture towards the ex-Premier League manager’s mother, who died soon after they met.

Ronaldo, 41, and Rodgers, 53, first met in the Prem when the former was a rising star at Manchester United and the latter was a coach at Chelsea.





After a game between the two Prem giants, the Northern Irish tactician asked the then United star if he could spare a few minutes to introduce him to his mum, who was his biggest fan.

The star forward graciously accepted and had a long talk with Mrs Rodgers with whom he also took commemorative pictures.

The ex-Liverpool boss’ mother sadly died in 2010 but he never forgot the Portugal captain’s kindness.

The two met again on Sunday in Saudi Arabia when Rodgers’ Al-Qadsiah defeated Ronaldo‘s Al-Nassr 3-1.



The Premier League icons shared a warm embrace before their Saudi Pro League clash and the ex-Leicester boss reminisced about their bond.

Rodgers said: “Our connection goes back a long way.

“When I was a young coach at Chelsea, my mother was at a Chelsea game against Manchester United and wanted to meet Ronaldo, who was her favourite player at the time, even though I worked for Chelsea.

“I spoke to Cristiano after the game to see if he could greet my mother, and he did.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“My mother is no longer with me, she passed away in 2010, but when he met her that day, it meant everything to me and, of course, it meant everything to her.

“So, he spent some time with her, took a picture, said very kind words to her, and that has always stayed with me.

“Our connection since that moment, obviously in the various clubs where I worked and where he played, has always remained strong.

“He’s a guy who’s done incredible things in his career, he’s probably the reason why so many people from Europe and all over the world are here in Saudi Arabia working.



“But I’ll never forget that moment, because it was a really special moment for my mother at the time and, obviously, for me, and I’ve never forgotten it.

“At that time, I was a young coach taking my first steps in the world of football and, obviously, I was at Chelsea working with fantastic players, but, at that time, Cristiano was a rising talent, a great figure.

“My mother loved football and, besides, she clearly knew what a good player he was.”

Rodgers left Chelsea in 2008 and started his managerial career with short spells at Watford as well as Reading.

He then rose to prominence at Swansea and after two impressive years in Wales he was signed by Liverpool where he almost won the Premier League in 2014.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, the Reds struggled the following season and that led to Rodgers being replaced by Jurgen Klopp.

But his career was revived shortly after with two successful spells at Celtic, where he won everything, and four impressive years at Leicester, where he won the FA Cup and Community Shield, before moving to Saudi Arabia.

Sports.title: Leeds manager Daniel Farke misses press conference with illness ahead of huge relegation clash
Sports.content:
LEEDS boss Daniel Farke missed Friday’s pre-match press conference with illness.

The German was confirmed as having been taken sick just hours before he was due to face the media to preview his team’s game against Tottenham.





A message from the club to journalists on the morning of the presser said: “Unfortunately due to illness, Daniel’s assistant Eddie Riemer will be taking today’s press conference.

“Daniel apologises and looks forward to seeing those of you at the game on Monday.”

Farke was due to fulfil his duties at 2.50pm on Friday.

Leeds know that they can mark themselves as officially safe from relegation with a point at Tottenham on Monday – if it isn’t confirmed before.



Even if they do not get a result, their place in the Premier League could be assured by the time the game kicks off.

They start the weekend in 14th, seven points clear of West Ham in 18th, with just nine still up for grabs.

Should the Hammers fail to beat Arsenal on Saturday evening, it would all but guarantee Leeds’ survival.

A loss would confirm Leeds are too far ahead, while a draw for West Ham would leave Leeds still needing a point at Spurs to be mathematically clear.



However, they also have a massive 14 goal difference advantage as well.

Farke’s men could leave their opponents in a tricky situation, though.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

If West Ham were to pull off a shock and beat Arsenal, Spurs would start Monday’s clash in the bottom three, trailing by two points, still another five (at least) from Nottingham Forest, who are also on the verge of safety.

Roberto De Zerbi, therefore, could find his side back in the drop zone with two matches to play.



Leeds, who beat Championship-bound Burnley 3-1 last weekend, have only lost four league games since December.

In that time, only Bournemouth and Manchester City (both one), Manchester United (two), and Arsenal (three) have lost fewer matches.

They also have a home clash with Brighton on May 17 and a final day meeting with none other than West Ham to round of the season.

Sports.title: Oliver Glasner admits Crystal Palace could hand Arsenal crucial title advantage on final day in Man City blow
Sports.content:
OLIVER GLASNER believes it would be “nonsense” to criticise him for playing a weakened team in a possible title decider.

But he warned Arsenal he could treat their final-day showdown as a “dress rehearsal” for the Conference League final.





Palace have their European final in Leipzig on May 27 – three days after hosting the Gunners at Selhurst Park in the last game of the Premier League season.

Glasner – whose side play Manchester City on Wednesday – fielded a full-strength team and drew against Arsenal three days before their crunch FA Cup semi-final a year ago.

Speaking ahead of Sunday’s clash with Everton, the Austrian said: “To be honest, if somebody criticises me, it would be nonsense.

“It’s just the last game but there are 37 games played before. That means if another team on matchday 25 rotated against City or Arsenal, they affected the title race as well.



“I’m not responsible for Arsenal and I’m not responsible for Manchester City.

“I’m responsible for Crystal Palace and I get paid for doing what’s best for Crystal Palace and not for City and not for Arsenal.

“I don’t know what we will do against Arsenal yet. Fortunately, I have time to think.

“Maybe we will treat it like a dress rehearsal and play the same line-up that we plan against Rayo Vallecano, that’s what we did at Frankfurt [before 2022 Europa League final].



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Again, a league title may feel like it’s decided on the last day but it’s the result of 38 matchdays and at the end everybody gets what they deserve.”

Glasner gave his players a day off on Friday after the euphoria of beating Shakhtar Donetsk in the Conference League semis.

But the Toffees game at home presents another significant opportunity.

Glasner added: “David Moyes is doing a fantastic job, they’re in the middle of the fight for European places but we want to win against Everton because then we are safe.



“We see all the teams at the bottom are winning and getting closer – Tottenham now have two wins in a row, West Ham and Nottingham Forest have been on very good runs.

“We are not 100 per cent safe so we need to get one more win.”

Sports.title: Football wag Apollonia Llewellyn almost bursts out of low-cut top as she puts on eye-popping display
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL Wag Apollonia Llewellyn left fans floored with her latest stunning social media post.

The blonde bombshell, famously known as ‘Barbi’, risked a major wardrobe malfunction as she squeezed into a black low-cut top.





Taking to her Instagram stories, the ring girl stunner sent temperatures soaring as she enjoyed some sun in a sizzling mirror selfie.

Barnsley-born Apollonia, 25, was bringing fans along for a trip to Los Angeles, United States.

The influencer’s eye-popping display saw her showing off points of her trip as she went through customs and then went to tuck into a juicy burger at In-N-Out.

Another snap showed off a dazzling blue sky alongside some palm trees with not a cloud in sight.

She then posed for a selfie with a Dr. Pepper in hand as she pouted her lips with some sunglasses on her head.

And she ended her flood of posts by teasing fans of what could be to come, thanks to a simple snap of a swimming pool.

Her army of more than 600,000 dedicated followers are often left picking their jaws up off the floor with her eye-popping posts.

Known for her high-profile roles in the world of boxing, as well as modelling for Playboy and Page 3, this latest look proved she is the ultimate undisputed queen of the ring.



But rather than looking for love with a king of the ring, she has found it with English footballer, Jai Rowe.

Last month she swapped the sun of LA for the light of her boyfriend as he starred for Raith Rovers during a 4-1 thrashing of Inverness in the Scottish Challenge Cup final.

Sports.title: Arne Slot claims 'no one will be positive' as he issues Liverpool reality check
Sports.content:
Arne Slot claims 'no one will be positive' as he issues Liverpool reality check

Arne Slot has presided over an underwhelming second season in charge of Liverpool and he knows that a winning end to the campaign won't change how people view them

View 2 Images Arne Slot has been bought back down to earth in his second year with Liverpool (Image: Visionhaus, Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Arne Slot accepts that "no one will be positive" about Liverpool's campaign and finishing with three wins won't change that perception.

‌



The Reds, who came into the season as defending champions, have fallen off their perch but look set to qualify for the Champions League, which was in doubt going back several weeks. They will finish the season by facing three sides in the top nine - starting with out-of-form Chelsea.

‌



Prior to losing at Manchester United last week Liverpool had won three on the bounce, and repeating that against the Blues, Aston Villa and Brentford would see them finish the year with six wins in seven.

‌



Yet the mid-season collapse, which saw them tumble down the table and out of title contention, has seen their season deemed underwhelming and Slot knows that won't change in the minds of many.

He said: "This season has been gone in a way that even if we have three wins and positive performances, I don't think anyone will be positive about the season. It's important we get at least one win over the line which might be enough.

Arne Slot confirms triple Liverpool return boost for Chelsea with Mo Salah update READ MORE :

"We are trying to do it in the best possible way, performance-wise. The positive thing is a few of the players who can be really important for us are either coming back at the weekend or after the weekend. That will help us.Three wins won't silence the criticism. Therefore we need to have a much longer run of result and performances."

‌



Liverpool's season has been all the more disappointing given the £400million plus investment they made into a squad that had claimed the title. A number of their major arrivals have come up short or struggled with form and fitness - Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz among them.

View 2 Images Liverpool had been tipped to challenge for the title, but they've been miles off the pace (Image: Michael Regan, Getty Images)

Slot though believes they have deserved more than they've got. "The performances, clearly in the Premier League, we didn't pick up the points we should have," said the Dutchman. "We haven't had a very good season in the Premier League but we've played better and not got the points we should have."

Article continues below

Despite the huge spend last summer Slot admits they will go again in the market, but claims the turnover will be be "as drastic" as it was 12 months ago. "There will be a bit of transition this summer but not as drastic as last summer," he said.

Sports.title: Luis Diaz shows Liverpool what they're missing as former team-mate speaks out on star
Sports.content:
Luis Diaz shows Liverpool what they're missing as former team-mate speaks out on star

One of Luis Diaz's former Liverpool teammates has reacted to the winger's form since joining Bayern Munich

View 2 Images Luis Diaz has flourished at Bayern Munich since leaving Liverpool (Image: ANP, ANP via Getty Images)

Thiago Alcantara has sung the praises of former Liverpool winger Luis Diaz following his move to Bayern Munich. The Colombian has been outstanding for the Bundesliga giants since completing his switch from Anfield last summer.

‌



The 29-year-old spent three-and-a-half years with the Reds, winning the Premier League, FA Cup and two League Cups. Diaz was a key figure in Arne Slot's title-winning side in 2025 but Liverpool have been forced to watch on as he takes his displays to another level in Munich.

‌



Given his prolific form, Liverpool may question whether selling Diaz was the right call. One of the winger's former teammates, Thiago has weighed in on the forward's season so far and backed Bayern's decision to snap up Diaz.

‌



"They're having a spectacular season. I think they made the right call signing Luis," Thiago told Sky Sport Deutschland.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I know him from Liverpool. He's a fantastic player and person. And Vinnie [Kompany] is doing a great job as coach.

‌



"The team is fantastic, with a very good mix of experienced and young players. It's a pleasure to watch them play."

Diaz has scored 26 goals and chipped in with 21 assists in 48 appearances for Bayern so far this season. This represents a considerable step up from his 41 goals and 23 assists in 148 outings for Liverpool, hinting that he may be hitting the peak of his powers.

The remarks from Thiago, who is Barcelona's assistant manager, shed light on the lasting impression the Colombian made during their time as teammates. The duo played together from January 2022 until the summer of 2024, when Thiago departed Anfield and subsequently hung up his boots.

‌



View 2 Images Thiago Alcantara spoke about his former teammate Luis Diaz (Image: Nick Taylor/Liverpool FC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

In February, reflecting on the choice to offload the Bayern star, Liverpool manager Slot said: "Luis Diaz is another example of how this club is run. If this club gets an offer like that for a 28-year-old, then this club, because it is built on sustainability, chooses to sell a player, and we are an exception in the Premier League, especially at the top of the Premier League, for that.

"That is why it is also so nice that we can achieve the things we have achieved in the last few years with that model. He is doing very well at Bayern, and that is not a surprise to me."

‌



Liverpool are expected to be on the hunt for wide players this summer. Mohamed Salah is poised to depart at the end of the campaign, while Slot may also look to strengthen his options down the left side.

Meanwhile, Bayern have already wrapped up the Bundesliga title this season, securing the championship with matches to spare. Vincent Kompany's men are also set to take on Stuttgart for the DFB-Pokal trophy but fell short of a place in the Champions League final after being knocked out at the semi-final stage by Paris Saint-Germain.

Sports.title: Frank Lampard receives shock approach over Premier League job despite Coventry promotion
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard receives shock approach over Premier League job despite Coventry promotion

Frank Lampard's stock has massively risen by virtue of leading Coventry to the Championship title and Crystal Palace are eyeing him up as Oliver Glasner's replacement

View 2 Images Lampard has led Coventry City back to the Premier League (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Crystal Palace have sounded out Frank Lampard about becoming their next manager with the Coventry boss' future in the Midlands by no means guaranteed despite their promotion.

‌



The 47-year-old has just led Coventry to the Championship title, ending their 25-year absence from the Premier League, but those exploits have caught the attention of the Eagles, who need to replace the outgoing Oliver Glasner.

‌



The Sun understands that they have made a move for Lampard, who has top flight experience with Chelsea and Everton, about taking over at Selhurst Park. Fulham themselves are also keen but need to see whether or not Marco Silva extends his contract.

‌



Lampard, who has also seen his name banded about regarding a third stint at Chelsea, is thought to be considering his options despite only just ending his promotion celebrations.

Coventry may have claimed the title, but there will naturally be doubts over whether they can remain a Premier League team long-term. Sky Blues owner Doug King is unlikely to have the resources to pour into the team and King himself has openly admitted that he may struggle to hang onto his manager this summer.

Frank Lampard details Pep Guardiola's help in guiding Coventry City to title READ MORE :

Lampard does have 12 months of his current contract to run and will be offered an improved deal, but it’s unlikely that King would stand in his way if he wanted to move elsewhere. Palace believe that under Lampard they can continue the success Glasner has brought to south London.

‌



The Eagles have been in the Premier League since 2013 and won last year's FA Cup. Glasner could yet go out on a high with the club into the final of the Europa Conference League, where they will play Rayo Vallecano in Leipzig later this month.

View 2 Images Crystal Palace are still looking for someone to replace Oliver Glasner

Palace were publicly criticised by Glasner for letting their top players leave after Eberechi Eze and Marc Guehi departed within six months of each other. But equally the club did spend in January, shelling out £78million to land Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen.

Article continues below

This season the trend of promoted sides going straight back down has been ended by Leeds and Sunderland. Prior to that, for two straight years, the three promoted teams all suffered immediate relegation back to the second tier.

Sports.title: Football club owners charged with human trafficking as ITV backtrack on planned show
Sports.content:
Football club owners charged with human trafficking as ITV backtrack on planned show

The co-owners of Maldon and Tiptree, Barrie Drewitt-Barlow and Scott Drewitt-Barlow, have been charged with human trafficking for sexual exploitation and rape following a police investigation

View 2 Images Scott Drewitt-Barlow and Barrie Drewitt-Barlow, the co-owners of Maldon & Tiptree, have been charged with human trafficking for sexual exploitation (Image: Getty Images)

Two co-owners of non-league football club Maldon and Tiptree have been charged with human trafficking for sexual exploitation and rape following an investigation by Essex Police.

Barrie Drewitt-Barlow, 57, was charged with multiple offences on Friday alongside Scott Drewitt-Barlow, 32. Both men, of Southwood Chase, Danbury, Essex, will appear at Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court later.

The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said the men have been charged with arranging or facilitating travel of another person with a view to exploitation, as well as sexual offences including rape. Barrie Drewitt-Barlow became Britain’s first gay surrogate parent in 1999.

The CPS said Barrie Drewitt-Barlow has been charged with three counts of sexual assault on a male, four counts of rape of a man 16 or over and two counts of arranging or facilitating travel of another person with a view to exploitation.

Scott Drewitt-Barlow has been charged with one count of sexual assault on a male, one count of rape of a man 16 or over, and two counts of arranging or facilitating travel of another person with a view to exploitation.

Arsenal handed new Premier League title advantage as Man City dealt double fixture blow READ MORE :

Luke Littler sends clear Man Utd transfer message after Real Madrid statement READ MORE :

Essex Police said officers from the Serious Crime Directorate carried out co-ordinated searches at premises in Danbury, Maldon and Braintree on Wednesday and arrested two men. The force said that since then they have been liaising with the Crown Prosecution Service.

Article continues below

Meanwhile, a polling station at the Drewitt-Barlow Stadium was relocated elsewhere because of “an ongoing police investigation”.

On Thursday, Doug Wilkinson, deputy returning officer for Maldon District Council, said: “In light of an ongoing police investigation, I have made the decision to relocate the polling station from the Drewitt-Barlow Stadium to Blackwater Leisure Centre.

View 2 Images ITV had planned to release a show about the club's co-owners, but that has now been shelved (Image: PA)

“Voters who were due to be voting at the Drewitt-Barlow Stadium, will be re-directed to Blackwater Leisure Centre and we apologise for any inconvenience this may cause due to the very late change.”

ITV has shelved a planned TV show about the men’s move into football club ownership. A press release on the ITV website published on March 31 and still available online on Friday morning said six-part series Up The Jammers “follows Barrie and Scott’s pursuit to take the Isthmian League North Division team to the grand heights of the English Football League within four years”.

The press release said: “Barrie wants sparkle, Scott’s in charge of making it happen – Anfield turf, glam loos, Guinness on tap for less than a fiver. But it turns out fans don’t just want fancy, they want three points.”

A quote from Barrie Drewitt-Barlow included in the press release said: “We didn’t get into football to play it safe, we got into it to build something big, and ITV is the perfect platform to bring that story to life. Nothing has been hidden. The pressure, the decisions, the ambition, the ups and downs, it’s all there. This is the reality of football ownership, unfiltered, and people are going to see exactly what it takes to try and take a club to the next level.”

On Friday morning, an ITV spokesperson said: “ITV has decided to remove Up The Jammers from the upcoming schedule. It will no longer be shown on ITV4 or ITVX as previously advertised.”

Sports.title: Prince William's admission about Prince George as future King shows his true colours
Sports.content:
Prince William's admission about Prince George as future King shows his true colours

Prince William's love for Aston Villa was on full display as they reached the Europa League final at Villa Park, where son George has been seen accompanying him before

View 2 Images Aston Villa fan Prince William was in attendance as his club reached the Europa League final (Image: Getty Images)

Aston Villa had royalty in the building as they powered their way into the Europa League final. And Prince William was unabashed in his support for the club as Unai Emery's men roared to within 90 minutes of continental silverware on Thursday.

‌



Having lost the opening leg of their semi-final 1-0, Villa redeemed themselves with a 4-0 hammering of Nottingham Forest in the return fixture. Their reward is a Europa League decider against Freiburg on May 20 after the Bundesliga outfit edged past Braga.

‌



An English team will feature in each of this season's three European finals in a proud campaign for the Premier League. Arsenal will contest the Champions League against titleholders Paris Saint-Germain, while Crystal Palace will meet Rayo Vallecano in the Conference League crescendo.

‌



But Villa die-hard Prince William only had eyes for what transpired at Villa Park as he watched his side earn their vengeance over Forest. Two goals from John McGinn topped off a historic night following earlier goals from Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Buendia, with the heir to the throne doing little to hide his glee.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

As for his children, Prince William has taken a hands-off approach and will not force his own fandom on any of his offspring. Prince George attended last year's Champions League clash away to PSG with his dad, but the future King later told TNT Sports pundit Rio Ferdinand he wouldn't make any demands.

‌



Aston Villa hammer hapless Nottingham Forest to reach Europa League final in style READ MORE :

How Prince William played key role in convincing Aston Villa cult hero to complete transfer READ MORE :

When quizzed on whether he would push his son to support Villa, Prince William insisted he wouldn't meddle. And not just in George's case; he would grant all his children the freedom to back whichever team they wanted.

"I’m genuinely open to whoever they support," he said. "I’m a bit biased but also they come to Villa games so they’re probably going to support Villa. I’ve left the other two at home tonight so we’ll wait and see who they support."

View 2 Images Prince William insisted he and the Princess of Wales' children are free to support whomever they like (Image: Mark Cuthbert/UK Press via Getty Images)

‌

The Prince of Wales has said in the past he grew up with friends who supported Villa and joined the bandwagon. He has also said he prioritised supporting a mid-table team that would assure more "rollercoaster, emotional moments."

It just so happens the 43-year-old was born less than a month after Villa's last continental triumph. They toppled Bayern Munich in Rotterdam in May 1982, shortly before the late Princess Diana gave birth to her first child.

The first Villa fixture Prince William attended was an FA Cup semi-final win over Bolton in 2000. They won that fixture on penalties and advanced to meet Chelsea in the final, where they were edged out by a lone goal from Roberto Di Matteo.

Sports.title: Double Arsenal injury update as Mikel Arteta drops 'no chance' remark for West Ham
Sports.content:
Double Arsenal injury update as Mikel Arteta drops 'no chance' remark for West Ham

Mikel Arteta has provided the latest Arsenal team news ahead of the Premier League clash against West Ham United

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta has delivered a new Arsenal injury update ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash at West Ham United (Image: (Photo by Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has revealed that Mikel Merino and Jurrien Timber have "no chance" of featuring against West Ham United this weekend.

‌



The Gunners duo have been unavailable for numerous weeks each, and while their exact return date is unclear, Arteta did at least confirm that no fresh injuries have been suffered.

‌



Speaking on Merino and Timber, he said: "No chance for them this weekend." When asked if either will play again this season, he replied: "I don't know there is still a fair bit to do. Everything needs to be so smooth and quick."

‌



Discussing Timber's ankle injury further and if it has proven to be a more complicated problem than expected, Arteta added: "Yes and that has probably been the most difficult thing to manage, with the player, with myself as well.

"We didn't expect it to take so long and he's not fit to play."

Arsenal can save a whopping £21m as Mikel Arteta turns attention to talented midfielder READ MORE :

John Terry digs out Arsenal stars for over-celebrating AGAIN after Champions League win READ MORE :

Merino has been absent since injuring his foot in the 3-2 defeat to Manchester United in January, while Timber has missed Arsenal's last 11 matches after suffering the ankle issue in the 2-0 win against Everton in March.

The Gunners head to West Ham looking to put one hand on the Premier League trophy. Dependent on Manchester City's result against Brentford on Saturday, Arteta's side could all-but secure their first top-flight title in 22 years should they travel to the London Stadium and claim all three points.

Sports.title: John Terry digs out Arsenal stars for over-celebrating AGAIN after Champions League win
Sports.content:
John Terry digs out Arsenal stars for over-celebrating AGAIN after Champions League win

Arsenal made only their second ever Champions League final on Tuesday night but John Terry felt their reaction at full-time was excessivde as he accused them of over-celebrating

View 2 Images Arsenal saw off Atletico Madrid on Tuesday to make the Champions League final (Image: UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

John Terry has claimed that Arsenal's celebrations were "a little bit too much for me" after they lapped up making the Champions League final.

‌



The Gunners saw off Atletico Madrid in their semi-final second-leg with Bukayo Saka's first-half strike proving decisive. The winger scored the only goal of the night, which saw the Premier League side pick up a 2-1 aggregate victory.

‌



It keeps alive their hopes of winning the Premier League and the Champions League, but their celebrations at full-time at the Emirates have been called out. The north Londoners had only ever been to one European Cup final, that back in 2006, whilst this current crop of stars are trying to end a six-year trophy drought.

‌



For several years Arsenal have been targeted by some former players and pundits for, what they perceive, to be over celebrating. Terry has again gone at Mikel Arteta's side.

He took to TikTok whilst watching PSG against Bayern Munich and said: "I’ve been looking forward to this game all week, especially after the poor game of football last night [between Arsenal and Atletico Madrid].

Arsenal can save a whopping £21m as Mikel Arteta turns attention to talented midfielder READ MORE :

Arsenal handed new Premier League title advantage as Man City dealt double fixture blow READ MORE :

"But fair play to Arsenal on making the Champions League final. What a game, what a start to the game this was tonight. How PSG have still got 11 men on the pitch I do not know. How PSG have not given away a penalty I do not know. It stinks of Chelsea versus Barcelona 2009/10 at Stamford Bridge where we should have had four or five penalties at least, but great game of football.

‌



"By the way, Arsenal way over-celebrated. Far too much for me. Yeah, you’re excited because you make the Champions League final, but over-celebrated a little bit too much for me."

View 2 Images John Terry has called out Arsenal's celebrations (Image: Crystal Pix/MB Media)

Terry made similar comments when Arsenal beat his former side Chelsea to reach the Carabao Cup final - a match they would ultimately lose to Manchester City. The Gunners beat the Blues in both games to secure a 4-2 aggregate win, but the former defender claims they over did it with their reaction.

Article continues below

"I just want to talk on Arsenal’s celebrations after… let’s not forget, it’s the Carabao Cup, it’s not the Champions League final," said Terry. "They celebrated far too much for me, I think that showed the pressure that’s on them at the moment."

Sports.title: Arsenal and Man City sent Crystal Palace rotation message by Oliver Glasner
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Man City sent Crystal Palace rotation message by Oliver Glasner

Crystal Palace could rotate against Manchester City and Arsenal in preparation for their UEFA Conference League final against Rayo Vallecano in Leipzig on May 27

View 2 Images Oliver Glasner claims he will "do what's best for Crystal Palace" before their Conference League final

Oliver Glasner has refused to rule out rotating his Crystal Palace side against Manchester City and Arsenal - but he insists his team selections will not define the Premier League title race.

‌



The Eagles have four top-flight matches left to play before facing Rayo Vallecano in the Conference League final in Leipzig on May 27.

‌



Glasner wants to minimise the risk of sustaining injuries and will juggle his side accordingly, even if it sparks backlash.

‌



He said: "To be honest, if somebody criticises for me, sorry, if I can say this, it would be nonsense.

"It's just the last game but there were 37 games played before. That means if another team on matchday 25 rotated against City or Arsenal they affected the title race as well.

Arsenal can save a whopping £21m as Mikel Arteta turns attention to talented midfielder READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta receives grovelling apology after TV presenter claimed he deserved a 'punch' READ MORE :

"I'm not responsible for Arsenal, I'm not responsible for Manchester City, I'm responsible for Crystal Palace and I get paid for doing the best things for Crystal Palace and not for City and not for Arsenal.

‌



"Again, I don't know what we're doing yet. Maybe we'll be playing with the same line-up that we'll play against Vallecano but again, maybe it feels like the league title is decided on the last day but at the end, it's a result of 38 matchdays and everybody gets what they deserve."

Palace travel to City next Wednesday before playing host to Arsenal on the final day at Selhurst Park.

Before Glasner even reaches his team selection predicament, he wants to ensure the club's Premier League status is confirmed and victory at home to Everton on Sunday would do exactly that.

‌



View 2 Images Crystal Palace play Arsenal on the final day of the season

He continued: "First of all we want to win against them because then we are safe. We see all the teams at the bottom are winning, Tottenham have two wins in a row.

"Nottingham [Forest] was on a very good run so all these teams are now closer and we are not 100 per cent safe.

‌



"That means one more win and then we can think about the Conference League.

"Again, I don't know right now how we will plan this because it's also the first time for me playing the last league game on Sunday and then Wednesday.

"When I was at Frankfurt, the last league game was on Saturday and we headed into the last practise needing to show something. We played the same team that we played in the [ Europa League ] final as the last test.

Article continues below

"I don't know if this makes sense if we play Sunday and Wednesday. Fortunately I have a bit of time to think about it and do my research and talk with my staff and then we will plan the last week but now it's really getting the win against Everton to be really safe in the league and then making the second step."

Sports.title: Exeter Chiefs approve takeover by Bournemouth owners
Sports.content:
Shareholders of Prem Rugby side Exeter Chiefs have approved takeover talks with the American owners of Premier League club Bournemouth.

Exeter members and shareholders gathered at a meeting on Thursday, at which they voted by a majority to permit the sale of the company to Cannae Holdings Inc's (Black Knight Sports and Entertainment).

Exeter chairman and chief executive Tony Rowe said: "This does not represent a firm offer.

"It is just a non-binding expression of interest at this stage but, hopefully, an offer will follow and we can begin negotiating the terms of the sale."

Exeter confirmed that any offer will be dependent on a 60-day due diligence process that will not be completed before the end of May.

Black Knight also hold a stake in French football club FC Lorient and own New Zealand side Auckland FC.

The announcement comes just days after Exeter's neighbours Cornish Pirates, who play in the second-tier Champ, announced American firm Stonewood Capital ​Management as investors in the club.

Exeter could become the third Prem team to receive significant investment across the last year, with Newcastle having been bought by Red Bull last August, and billionaire Sir James Dyson having put funding into Bath in March.

Sports.title: Littler: I'm not even practising but I'm getting in my rivals' heads
Sports.content:
Luke Littler has revealed he's "not practising" at the moment despite three nightly Premier League Darts wins on the trot, adding he feels he is getting in rivals Luke Humphries and Michael van Gerwen's heads.

Littler made it a hat-trick of nightly wins on Thursday, claiming a record-equalling sixth of the 2026 Premier League season as he beat Humphries 6-5 in the final on Night 14 in Leeds.

The 19-year-old also saw off Van Gerwen by the same narrow 6-5 margin in his Thursday quarter-final, in addition to beating Jonny Clayton 6-5 in the semi-finals.

The Nuke's nightly win comes a week after he beat Humphries by the same 6-5 scoreline to win Night 13 in Aberdeen.

"I've said for many years, I always back myself in a last leg," Littler said.

Image: Littler says he feels repeat last-leg wins over rivals Humphries and Michael van Gerwen means he is getting in their heads

"I just say to myself: 'It's do or die, you've got to hit it' - and that's what I did. Again with Luke [Humphries], same as last week, his worst leg was that last one. But yeah, another nightly win.

"Obviously taking out any big shot is always a good feeling. The one against Michael [Van Gerwen] was probably the biggest shot I've hit this year (fifth leg 141 checkout). It was good to see Michael battling again. Then to get past Jonny [Clayton] and past Luke, I think the next two weeks are going to be very interesting and I'll be watching along.

"Obviously beating them [Humphries, Van Gerwen] numerous times in last-leg deciders over the years helps me. It might be in their heads: 'Hang on a minute, it's me against Luke Littler in another last-leg decider'.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Humphries checked out 132 followed by a 146 from Littler in Leeds

"I might already have won over them before that leg even starts. Ever since the JDC (Junior Darts Corporation) days, I've always backed myself, and I think I produce really well in deciding legs.

"Whether you beat them comfortably or in a last leg, it's always on the mind.

"Obviously the record with Gezzy [Gerwen Price] is a pretty even one, and me and Luke [Humphries] beat each other all the time, same with me and Michael. But if I keep getting these wins week in, week out, it gives me a lot of confidence. Then when they next face me, they know they've got to produce even better."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler took out a crucial 141 to clinch the fifth leg in the Premier League Darts quarter-final against Van Gerwen in Leeds

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Premier League Night 14 match between Littler and Van Gerwen.

Thursday night saw Littler's preparations heavily disrupted too as he turned up at the venue less than an hour before his quarter-final against Van Gerwen due to being delayed in traffic.

Yet, the double reigning world champion managed to push through to claim three more victories. And he did so despite the fact he is not practising at the moment.

"I think I'm playing very well," Littler says. "The last three weeks have been wins, and that's all down to me and the right preparation.

"I can say when I've been at home, I've not really been practising, but that's just what I do. I'll turn up here, have a few hours if that, and then produce it on stage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Littler set another record by winning three nights in a row and has his eyes set on history

"I think the most nightly wins is definitely one to go for. It's a long old night with the three games, but I've done it numerous times before. Hopefully I can break my own record.

"I think it's [booing] always going to come, and this is what I've got to do, just keep winning and keep winning. Eventually, hopefully they'll get bored of me because nothing's really working. Ever since Rotterdam, even tonight, there were a few boos, but nothing will ever top that. I think I can battle past anything now."

Sports.title: Bournemouth drop Jimenez amid investigation into social media posts
Sports.content:
Bournemouth statement: "AFC Bournemouth are aware of posts circulating on social media involving right-back, Alex Jimenez. The club understand the seriousness of the matter and it is currently being investigated."

Bournemouth have released a statement confirming they have dropped Alex Jimenez from their game against Fulham this weekend

Bournemouth have released a statement confirming they have dropped Alex Jimenez for their game against Fulham this weekend.

The club say this is in relation to an investigation into posts circulating on social media, which they describe as being of a serious nature.

The statement reads: "AFC Bournemouth are aware of posts circulating on social media involving right-back, Alex Jimenez.

"The club understand the seriousness of the matter and it is currently being investigated.

"As a result, Alex will not be included in the squad for tomorrow's Premier League game against Fulham and the club will be making no further comment at this time."

Sky Sports News has attempted to contact representatives of Jimenez for comment.

Jimenez, who turned 21 on Friday, has made 32 appearances for Bournemouth this season after a summer loan switch from AC Milan.

The move to Vitality Stadium was made permanent in February.

Sports.title: Why Spurs have the edge on West Ham in two-way relegation scrap
Sports.content:
And then there were two. It seems either West Ham or Tottenham will be the final team relegated from the Premier League this season, and, with three games to go, their next matches – both live on Sky Sports – could be decisive in the fight for survival.

Back-to-back wins for Spurs under Roberto De Zerbi has flipped the narrative and pulled them out of the bottom three, where West Ham currently reside, but by the time Tottenham face Leeds on Monday night they could be back in the drop zone.

The Hammers, currently one point adrift of Spurs, would have to beat title favourites Arsenal, who have turned a corner themselves of late, to usurp their rivals, while a repeat of last weekend's defeat at Brentford could prove fatal.

Mathematically, nothing can be decided in this next round of fixtures, but if Spurs open up a four-point gap, then Nuno Espirito Santo's side will find themselves with very little room for manoeuvre and relying on two slip ups from their rivals in their final two games.

Remaining PL fixtures Tottenham: Leeds (H), Chelsea (A), Everton (H)

West Ham: Arsenal (H), Newcastle (A), Leeds (H)

What does Opta's supercomputer say?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Tottenham Hotspur.

There was a big swing in the relegation probabilities after the last round of games as West Ham lost 3-0 at Brentford on Saturday before Spurs produced their most convincing performance of 2026 the following day to win 2-1 at Aston Villa and move out of the bottom three.

Opta's supercomputer is currently projecting West Ham as having more than 80 per cent chance of going down, while Spurs are at 19.3 per cent, which is some turnaround from a week ago.

At the beginning of May, before the win at Villa, Spurs were deemed to have a 59 per cent chance of being relegated but that has shot down, while West Ham's have gone sharply in the other direction. Their chances of going down have more than doubled since then.

There is still an outside chance of Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace or Leeds United slipping back into the bottom three. Opta is currently projecting them as having less than a one per cent chance of going down.

Mathematically, 13th-placed Newcastle could still be relegated, but it would require them losing every game and West Ham winning every game as well as a goal difference swing of 17.

What does the form tell us?

This has become one of the most competitive Premier League relegation battles of the last two decades, which makes it much harder to predict what is going to happen in the final few weeks of the season.

Recent results at the bottom more closely resemble a title race than a relegation scrap.

Despite the defeat at Brentford, West Ham have been the sixth best team in the Premier League since January 17, when they defeated Spurs 1-0 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, and they are closely followed by Nottingham Forest.

Spurs' turnaround has been more recent, thanks to the arrival of De Zerbi, and in the four games he has overseen, they have been in the top half for form, picking up seven points, the same total as West Ham over that period.

The form table somewhat challenges the idea that West Ham have a much tougher matchup in their next game.

In Leeds, Spurs are playing the second-best team in the Premier League over those last four matches and the fourth-best team over the last six matches, a period in which Daniel Farke's side have gone unbeaten.

Two of Leeds' wins over that period came against the relegated teams, Burnley and Wolves, but they handled both with ease and claimed a big win against third-placed Manchester United, their first at Old Trafford since 1981. They are not to be underestimated.

Arsenal sit below Leeds - as well as Spurs and West Ham - in the form table over the last four games. They have faced a tougher schedule and appear to have overcome their momentary wobble, but it shows the Gunners are there to be got at.

West Ham also have recent form for denting Arsenal's title bids, drawing 2-2 at the London Stadium in 2023 when Bukayo Saka missed a penalty, and inflicting a 1-0 defeat on the Gunners at the Emirates Stadium in February 2025.

Who has the toughest fixtures?

Only Crystal Palace and Brentford are deemed to have a harder schedule than West Ham by Opta for the Premier League run-in – and their next match is the hardest of them all.

It is never a good time to play the Premier League leaders, but at crunch time in the season, with a first title in more than two decades on the line, this seems to be the worst possible time to be playing Arsenal, who are just three wins from ending their drought.

Especially when you consider the momentum behind Mikel Arteta's side, fresh from defeating Atletico Madrid to reach their first Champions League final for 20 years, and a win over Fulham which showed a return to the formidable form that has brought them here.

West Ham, who are effectively two points adrift of Spurs because of their inferior goal difference, then face a trip to Newcastle before welcoming Leeds to the London Stadium on the final day.

In comparison, Spurs are rated as having the eighth easiest schedule in the Premier League, with Monday's game against Leeds followed by a trip to out-of-form Chelsea, who have lost their last six games in the competition, and a home game against Everton.

How many points needed for survival?

The Opta supercomputer projects 40 points to be enough to secure Premier League survival. In the last nine Premier League seasons, teams finishing on 36 points or more have avoided relegation, which is exactly where West Ham are right now.

Last season, 26 points would have been enough to stay up as an exceptionally poor bottom three of Leicester, Ipswich and Southampton all made an immediate return to the Championship.

Spurs took advantage of the trio's weaknesses to focus on winning the Europa League as they finished a dismal 17th on 38 points - 13 points above 18th-placed Leicester.

But that luxury for Tottenham is not there this season as they face the very real possibility of relegation to the second tier of English football for the first time since 1977.

Only three teams have been relegated with 40 points or more in the 20-team Premier League era - Sunderland (1996/97), Bolton (1997/98) and West Ham (2002/03) - the latter holding the record for the team relegated with the most points with 42.
